name: Goji berry (Lycium barbarum)
short: Case reports: bleeding and very high INR on warfarin after goji juice, raised INR after goji tea; allergy, including anaphylaxis. 90-day trial of a milk-based product: no related adverse events.
text: Case reports describe raised INR values in women taking warfarin after drinking goji: a 71-year-old woman was hospitalised with a markedly elevated INR (prothrombin time over 120 seconds), nosebleeds, bruising and rectal bleeding after 4 days of goji juice, which the authors rated a probable interaction, and a 61-year-old woman previously stable on warfarin had an INR of 4.1 after 4 days of a concentrated tea made from Lycium barbarum fruits; in laboratory tests the tea only weakly inhibited the enzyme that breaks down warfarin, so the authors suggested other mechanisms may be involved. A systematic review of food, herb and supplement interactions with warfarin lists Chinese wolfberry among those with an increased risk of bleeding (across all the foods, herbs and supplements it reviewed, not goji specifically, reported bleeding ranged from minor events to intracranial bleeding that led to death), and a review of goji found no signs of toxicity of the plant but said the warfarin cases point to a potential risk of drug interaction. One report describes two cases of allergic reaction after eating goji berries, one of them anaphylactic, which seemed to involve lipid transfer proteins that cross-react with tomato; in a Spanish study of 31 people with plant-food allergies, 24 (77%) had positive skin tests to goji berries: 5 of them had symptoms and 19 did not, but most of the study's patients had never eaten goji berries (20 of the 30 recruited after a first patient reacted, against 6 who had eaten them without symptoms); the authors concluded that goji berries have allergenic potential in people with food allergy, especially those allergic to lipid transfer protein. In a 90-day randomised placebo-controlled trial in 150 healthy people aged 65 to 70, a milk-based goji berry formulation was not associated with any product-related adverse events.
